title: McGreevy struggles as Brewers hand Cardinals a 6-0 loss in Milwaukee
text:
Michael McGreevy, a right-handed pitcher for the St. Louis Cardinals, faced challenges on May 27 during a 6-0 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field. Despite entering the game with strong statistics this season, McGreevy allowed seven hits and five runs—his highest total of the year—while striking out six batters.
McGreevy is known for his unique approach on the mound, relying on sequencing and accuracy rather than high velocity or movement. Before Tuesday’s game, he had allowed two earned runs or fewer in seven of his ten starts and had consistently pitched into the sixth inning. However, advanced analytics indicated some underlying concerns: his expected ERA was 5.84 before Tuesday’s outing, placing him in the ninth percentile among pitchers. His expected batting average against (.296), whiff rate (19.4%), barrel percentage (10%), and chase percentage (28.4%) were also below league averages.
During Tuesday’s game, McGreevy struggled with execution and command issues not typically seen from him this season. He said after the game that his sinker did not have its usual movement: “It’s not that I want that sinker back to Contreras in that fifth inning, but I think if the shape is normal, how I normally throw my sinker and how it normally is, that’s a groundball double play, take two [outs] for one [run]. But I just have to be better. … I was committed with the changeup, but it was one of those days where it was moving a little bit differently.”
Back-to-back walks following a leadoff double further highlighted his uncharacteristic control problems during a pivotal fifth inning when William Contreras hit a two-run double off McGreevy’s diminished sinker to extend Milwaukee’s lead.
Despite these setbacks in only his 30th career start, McGreevy remains focused on learning from each outing as he refines his pitch mix and adapts to major league hitters multiple times through an order. “I think being a professional and trying to be a good starter in this league, I have to understand the shape is what it is today… Chop it up to a learning lesson, you know,” he said.
